newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: GOLF-BRILLIANT START PUSHES LEHMAN INTO LEAD.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BRILLIANT START PUSHES LEHMAN INTO LEAD.

text.p: British Open champion Tom Lehman started his third round of the South Australian Open brilliantly on Saturday to set up a one-stroke lead over Australia's Wayne Grady.
The world number two picked up three shots in his first two holes before going on to card a six-under-par 66 for a total of 13-under 203.
Grady, a former U.S. PGA champion, fired his second successive round of 66 to be one shot clear of fellow-Australians Peter O'Malley and Greg Chalmers.
Lehman birdied the par-four first hole and then made an eagle three on the second hole for the American to leapfrog up the leaderboard after being two strokes off the lead overnight.
The only blemish for Lehman came with a bogey five at the ninth hole. He immediately regrouped with a birdie at the 10th hole and picked up further shots at the 12th, 16th and 17th.

Despite his rousing third round performance Lehman later told reporters he thought the benign conditions at the Kooyonga Golf Club course meant an even better score would be necessary on Sunday to win the tournament.
"I think somebody could shoot 62 here," Lehman said. "If I look at my rounds, I know there's been the potential for a low round like that.
"If the course stays like this it's going to take a real low score by somebody. You have to...keep the pedal to the metal," he said.

O'Malley and Chalmers challenged for the lead throughout the third round, both carding rounds of 67. Chalmers was on course to share second with Grady before he missed a short putt for par on the 18th hole.

Overnight leaders Michael Long of New Zealand and Michael Harwood of Australia both fired 72s to drop four places down the leaderboard. Harwood equalled the course record with a round of 65 on Friday.
